title: Position Bias Correction is Insufficient for One-Pass Attention Sorting

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to enable single-pass document reordering that aims to match the performance of expensive iterative attention sorting. Paper [2] ("LongRanker: Efficient One-Pass Document Reranking with Long-Context Large Language Models") explicitly addresses efficient one-pass document reranking, aiming to reduce computational overhead compared to iterative methods. This aligns substantively with the contribution's purpose of achieving efficient single-pass reordering.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves estimating a position-bias curve from distractor documents, trimming top-alpha attention, binning positions, taking median attention, interpolating, and subtracting the bias from raw attention scores. Paper [15] ("LLM-Based Listwise Reranking Under the Effect of Positional Bias") proposes DebiasFirst, which mitigates positional bias in LLM-based reranking by addressing architectural and input positioning biases. While the specific implementation details differ, both mechanisms share the underlying primitive of correcting positional bias in attention scores to improve ranking. Paper [28] ("Lost in the Middle at Birth: An Exact Theory of Transformer Position Bias") also discusses positional bias correction, focusing on the inherent geometric properties of attention mechanisms. These papers cover the mechanism at the primitive level.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates its method on SynthWiki@28K using two models, comparing the cost of single-pass attention sorting (2 prefills) to iterative sorting (6 prefills for k=5). Paper [14] ("Attention Sorting Combats Recency Bias In Long Context Language Models") evaluates attention sorting methods in long-context LLMs, using benchmarks to assess positional bias mitigation. Paper [15] ("LLM-Based Listwise Reranking Under the Effect of Positional Bias") evaluates positional bias correction methods using diagnostic metrics and benchmarks. Both papers reuse evaluation designs that involve position bias metrics and long-context LLM benchmarks, covering the evaluation facet.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of long-context retrieval and document reranking for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Paper [1] ("Embedding-Based Context-Aware Reranker") and Paper [2] ("LongRanker: Efficient One-Pass Document Reranking with Long-Context Large Language Models") both address document reranking in RAG systems, covering the same general application area. While the specific dataset (SynthWiki@28K) is new, this is a change of instance, not a new domain.
